_meta.note: Substitutions work best in most recipes but can affect texture. Never guarantee allergy-safe substitutions.
_meta.disclaimer: Sam offers substitutions as a starting point. Not medical or allergy advice.

free.substitute: 1 cup milk + 1 tablespoon white vinegar or lemon juice. Stir and let sit 5 minutes.
1 tablespoon ground flaxseed + 3 tablespoons water. Mix and let sit 5 minutes to thicken.
free.notes: Works for cookies, muffins, quick breads. Not for airy or leavened bakes.
Cake will be more moist. Not ideal for cookies where creaming matters.
Cookies spread more and taste less rich.

free.substitute: 1 cup white sugar + 1 tablespoon molasses (for light) or 2 tablespoons (for dark). Mix well.
3/4 cup + 2 tablespoons all purpose flour + 2 tablespoons cornstarch. Sift twice.
free.notes: The cornstarch lowers the protein like cake flour does.

free.substitute: 1 cup all purpose flour + 1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder + 1/4 teaspoon salt
free.notes: Use immediately, don't store the mix.

free.substitute: 1/4 teaspoon baking soda + 1/2 teaspoon cream of tartar

free.notes: Won't whip. Fine for sauces, ganache, baked goods.
For baking only. Won't taste right in coffee or on cereal.
Mild flavor swap. Works in most cookies and cakes.

free.substitute: 3 tablespoons cocoa powder + 1 tablespoon butter or oil
3/4 cup brown sugar + 1/4 cup water. Warm to dissolve.

free.notes: Changes color and flavor slightly. Fine for most baking.

free.substitute: There is no true substitute. For quick breads only: use baking powder or a combo of baking soda + acid.
free.notes: Real yeast breads need the real thing. Hmm.

free.substitute: 2 teaspoons lemon juice or white vinegar
free.notes: Works for meringues and some acid uses.

pro.substitute: 1 cup oat milk
pro.notes: 1:1 swap. Oat milk browns well and is the closest to whole milk in bakes.

pro.substitute: 1 cup unsweetened soy milk
pro.notes: 1:1 swap. Highest protein of the plant milks, so it browns and sets best.

pro.substitute: 1 cup unsweetened almond milk
pro.notes: 1:1 swap. Thinner than dairy milk, so crumb can be slightly drier.

pro.substitute: 1 cup unsweetened soy milk plus 1 tablespoon lemon juice. Stir and rest 5 minutes.
pro.notes: Soy curdles best. Rice and almond milk stay thin but still add the acid.

pro.substitute: 1 cup vegan block butter
pro.notes: 1:1 swap. Use block, not tub spread, which holds too much water for pastry.

pro.substitute: 8 oz dairy free cream cheese, or 1 cup raw cashews soaked 4 hours and blended with 1 tablespoon lemon juice
pro.notes: Cashew version is thicker. Chill before frosting so it pipes.

pro.substitute: 1 cup unsweetened coconut yogurt plus 1 teaspoon lemon juice
pro.notes: 1:1 swap. Adds a faint coconut note to lighter bakes.

pro.substitute: 1 cup unsweetened soy or coconut yogurt
pro.notes: 1:1 swap. Choose unsweetened or the bake turns cloying.

pro.substitute: 1 cup coconut cream, chilled overnight and the solid part whipped
pro.notes: Whips to soft peaks only. Keep it cold and it holds for a few hours.

pro.substitute: 8 oz cream cheese beaten with 1/4 cup heavy cream and 2 tablespoons softened butter
pro.notes: Close in richness. A little tangier than the real thing.

pro.substitute: 1 cup cottage cheese, blended smooth
pro.notes: 1:1 swap. Drain first if the cheese is very wet.

pro.substitute: 1 cup sour cream
pro.notes: 1:1 swap. Sour cream is tangier and splits at a higher heat, so keep it off the boil.

pro.substitute: 2 1/4 cups whole milk simmered gently down to 1 cup, then cooled
pro.notes: Takes about 25 minutes. Stir often so it does not catch.

pro.substitute: 1/2 cup whole milk plus 1/2 cup heavy cream
pro.notes: 1:1 once mixed. Works anywhere half and half is poured, not whipped.

pro.substitute: 1 cup measure for measure gluten free blend that already contains xanthan gum
pro.notes: Rest the batter 30 minutes so the starches hydrate. Check labels for cross contamination.

pro.substitute: 1 1/2 cups white rice flour, 3/4 cup potato starch, 1/2 cup tapioca starch, 1/4 cup brown rice flour, 2 teaspoons xanthan gum
pro.notes: Whisk thoroughly and store airtight. Use cup for cup in place of all purpose.

pro.substitute: 2 teaspoons whole psyllium husk
pro.notes: Psyllium gives a chewier, more bread like crumb. Add liquid slowly, it drinks more.

pro.substitute: 1 tablespoon ground chia soaked in 3 tablespoons water
pro.notes: Best in muffins and cookies. Leaves faint flecks.

pro.substitute: 1 1/4 cups rolled oats blended fine
pro.notes: Use certified gluten free oats if that matters for your bake.

pro.substitute: 1 cup pulsed gluten free crackers, or 1 cup rolled oats blitzed coarse
pro.notes: Toast briefly for colour, they brown more slowly than wheat crumbs.

pro.substitute: 1 1/2 cups crushed gluten free digestive style biscuits
pro.notes: Add an extra tablespoon of melted butter, gluten free crumbs bind loosely.

pro.substitute: 1 cup sunflower seed flour
pro.notes: 1:1 swap. Can turn faintly green next to baking soda, which is harmless.

pro.substitute: 1 cup fine cornmeal, or 1 cup durum flour
pro.notes: Cornmeal gives the same grit for dusting. Texture in doughs will be softer.

pro.substitute: 1 tablespoon ground chia plus 3 tablespoons water, rested 5 minutes
pro.notes: Binds like flax with a milder flavour. Best in dark or spiced bakes.

pro.substitute: 1/4 cup unsweetened applesauce
pro.notes: Adds moisture, not lift. Use in muffins and quick breads, up to two eggs worth.

pro.substitute: 1/4 cup mashed ripe banana
pro.notes: Adds moisture and banana flavour. Fine in spiced bakes, obvious in vanilla ones.

pro.substitute: 1/4 cup plain yogurt
pro.notes: Keeps the crumb tender. Does not leaven, so pair with a little extra baking powder.

pro.substitute: 1 teaspoon baking soda plus 1 tablespoon white vinegar, mixed in last
pro.notes: Purely for rise. Get it into the oven quickly, the fizz is short lived.

pro.substitute: 2 tablespoons aquafaba, the liquid from a tin of chickpeas
pro.notes: 1:1 by volume. Whips to stiff peaks with a pinch of cream of tartar.

pro.substitute: 3 tablespoons aquafaba
pro.notes: Works in cakes and brownies. Not in custards, which need the yolk to set.

pro.substitute: 1 tablespoon full fat yogurt plus 1 teaspoon oil
pro.notes: Covers the fat and the moisture. Will not thicken a custard on its own.

pro.substitute: 2 tablespoons milk, plant milk, cream, or aquafaba brushed thin
pro.notes: Milk browns softly, cream browns deepest, aquafaba gives the closest shine.

pro.substitute: 1 cup coconut sugar
pro.notes: 1:1 swap. Darkens the crumb and tastes faintly of caramel.

pro.substitute: 3/4 cup honey. Reduce other liquid by 2 tablespoons and drop the oven 25F.
pro.notes: Browns much faster. Keep an eye on the edges.

pro.substitute: 3/4 cup maple syrup. Reduce other liquid by 3 tablespoons.
pro.notes: Adds moisture and a clear maple note. Best in muffins and quick breads.

pro.substitute: 1 1/3 cups erythritol
pro.notes: About 70 percent as sweet. Does not caramelise, and can taste cooling.

pro.substitute: 1 cup monk fruit blend measured for baking
pro.notes: 1:1 for the blends cut with erythritol. Pure monk fruit is far sweeter, read the tin.

pro.substitute: 1 teaspoon liquid stevia plus 1/3 cup applesauce or yogurt to replace the bulk
pro.notes: Stevia sweetens but adds no body, so something has to fill the volume.

pro.substitute: 1 cup granulated sugar plus 1 tablespoon cornstarch, blended until floury
pro.notes: Let the dust settle before opening the blender. Sieve before icing.

pro.substitute: 1 cup granulated sugar pulsed briefly in a blender
pro.notes: Stop while it is still grainy. Blitzed too far it becomes powdered sugar.

pro.substitute: 1 cup granulated sugar plus 2 tablespoons molasses, rubbed together
pro.notes: Light brown uses 1 tablespoon instead. Rub with fingertips until evenly damp.

pro.substitute: 1/4 cup demerara sugar, or granulated sugar for a finer finish
pro.notes: For sprinkling. Granulated loses the crunch but keeps the sparkle.

pro.substitute: 1 cup plus 2 tablespoons butter
pro.notes: The extra covers the water in butter. Spread is slightly wider, flavour better.

pro.substitute: 1 cup melted and cooled butter
pro.notes: 1:1 swap. Richer flavour, marginally firmer crumb once cool.

pro.substitute: 1/2 cup oil plus 1/2 cup unsweetened applesauce
pro.notes: Replace half at most. All applesauce turns the crumb gummy.

pro.substitute: 1 cup shortening, or 1 cup butter for flavour
pro.notes: Shortening matches the texture. Butter browns better but holds less flake.

pro.substitute: 1 cup butter, or 1 cup neutral oil
pro.notes: 1:1 either way. Butter for flavour, oil for a softer set at room temperature.

pro.substitute: 1 cup clarified butter, or 1 cup butter with the recipe liquid reduced by 2 tablespoons
pro.notes: Plain butter carries water, so the small reduction keeps the balance.

pro.substitute: 1 cup all purpose flour plus 1 teaspoon vital wheat gluten
pro.notes: Lifts the protein enough for a chewier crumb and a stronger rise.

pro.substitute: 2/3 cup all purpose flour plus 1/3 cup cake flour
pro.notes: Sits between the two in protein. Ideal for tender pie crust.

pro.substitute: 1 cup white whole wheat flour, or 1/2 cup whole wheat plus 1/2 cup all purpose
pro.notes: Swapping all of it makes a denser loaf. Half and half is the safe bet.

pro.substitute: 1 cup whole wheat flour
pro.notes: Loses the rye tang. Add 1 teaspoon caraway to get some of it back.

pro.substitute: 1 tablespoon arrowroot, or 2 tablespoons all purpose flour
pro.notes: Arrowroot sets clearer and does not like long boiling. Flour goes cloudy.

pro.substitute: 1 tablespoon arrowroot or cornstarch
pro.notes: 1:1 swap. Tapioca gives the glossiest fruit fillings.

pro.substitute: 1 tablespoon cornstarch
pro.notes: 1:1 swap. Not the same as potato flour, which is far heavier.

pro.substitute: No true swap. Use bread flour in place of all purpose instead.
pro.notes: Nothing else adds protein this way. Adjust the flour rather than the additive.

pro.substitute: 3 teaspoons baking powder, and cut any acid in the recipe
pro.notes: Rise is weaker and can taste salty. Better to buy soda if you can.

pro.substitute: 2 1/4 teaspoons instant yeast, plus 1/2 cup flour and 1/2 cup water added to the dough
pro.notes: Ready in hours instead of a day. You lose the sour, so expect a milder loaf.

pro.substitute: 1 cup active starter, minus 1/2 cup flour and 1/2 cup water from the recipe
pro.notes: Give the dough far longer to rise. Watch the dough, not the clock.

pro.substitute: 1 tablespoon white vinegar
pro.notes: 1:1 for chemistry. Vinegar brings no citrus flavour, so skip it in lemon bakes.

pro.substitute: 1/2 cup natural cocoa, and swap the baking powder for 1/8 teaspoon baking soda per 1/2 cup
pro.notes: The two cocoas differ in acidity, so the leavener has to change with them.

pro.substitute: 1/2 cup Dutch process cocoa, and swap baking soda for 1 teaspoon baking powder
pro.notes: Going the other way needs the opposite leavener or the bake falls flat.

pro.substitute: 1 tablespoon cocoa powder plus 2 teaspoons sugar plus 2 teaspoons butter
pro.notes: Fine melted into batter. Will not temper or set as a coating.

pro.substitute: 6 oz chocolate bar, chopped
pro.notes: Chopped bar melts into pools rather than holding its shape. Usually an improvement.

pro.substitute: 2 teaspoons instant coffee granules, crushed fine
pro.notes: Weaker, so the doubling matters. Deepens chocolate without tasting of coffee.

pro.substitute: 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract plus a drop of amaretto if you have it
pro.notes: Nothing truly replaces it. Use less, almond is assertive.

pro.substitute: 1/2 teaspoon lemon extract, or 2 teaspoons dried lemon peel
pro.notes: Zest carries oils that extract cannot match. Add at the end for the brightest note.

pro.substitute: 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon, 1 teaspoon ginger, 1/2 teaspoon nutmeg, 1/4 teaspoon allspice, 1/4 teaspoon cloves
pro.notes: Mix and store airtight. Scales up neatly.

pro.substitute: 2 teaspoons cinnamon, 1/2 teaspoon nutmeg, 1/4 teaspoon allspice, 1/4 teaspoon cardamom
pro.notes: Softer and warmer than pumpkin spice. Good on anything with fruit.

pro.substitute: 1 cup liquid buttermilk, and hold back 1 cup of the recipe liquid
pro.notes: Powder exists to keep the mix dry, so only swap when the liquid can move.

pro.substitute: 1 cup all purpose flour
pro.notes: The same flour under two names. No adjustment needed.

pro.substitute: 1 cup bread flour
pro.notes: Same high protein flour. Straight swap.

pro.substitute: 1 cup superfine sugar, or granulated pulsed briefly
pro.notes: Dissolves faster than granulated, which matters in meringue and creaming.

pro.substitute: 1 cup powdered or confectioners sugar
pro.notes: Same thing. UK icing sugar sometimes has no cornstarch, so icing can set softer.

pro.substitute: 1 teaspoon baking soda
pro.notes: Identical. Only the name changes.

pro.substitute: 1 tablespoon cornstarch
pro.notes: Identical. Not to be confused with US cornflour, which is milled corn.

pro.substitute: 1 cup heavy cream
pro.notes: Double cream is richer at about 48 percent fat, so heavy cream whips a little softer.

pro.substitute: 1 cup light cream, or half and half
pro.notes: Too thin to whip either way. Fine for pouring and enriching.

pro.substitute: 1 cup light corn syrup, or 3/4 cup honey
pro.notes: Corn syrup matches the texture. Golden syrup has a buttery note honey mimics better.

pro.substitute: 1 cup molasses
pro.notes: Near enough identical. Treacle is a shade less bitter.

pro.substitute: 1 cup dark brown sugar
pro.notes: Muscovado is moister and stronger. Dark brown is the closest easy swap.

pro.substitute: 1 1/2 cups crushed graham crackers
pro.notes: Swap by volume of crumbs. Graham is a touch sweeter.

pro.substitute: 1 cup all purpose flour plus 1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder plus 1/4 teaspoon salt
pro.notes: Whisk thoroughly so the leavener is evenly spread.
